task_title: starlark-dsl guide matches shipped DSL: signatures, marshalling, json() encoder + drift guard
task_criteria: PROOF: go test -short -count=1 -run TestDslGuideBuiltinDrift ./internal/builtin/ passes at the integrated tip, and docs/guides/starlark-dsl.md contains the exact signatures http_get(url, headers=None) and json(value) plus a committed runnable example script demo/scripts/dsl-builtins.star making the three documented calls. FAILIF: the drift test is absent from internal/builtin/, or it passes while the guide omits any builtin signature that dsl run --help prints, or the guide names a builtin the binary does not ship.

items.criterion: PROOF: go test -short -count=1 -run TestDslGuideBuiltinDrift ./internal/builtin/ passes at the integrated tip, and docs/guides/starlark-dsl.md contains the exact signatures http_get(url, headers=None) and json(value) plus a committed runnable example script demo/scripts/dsl-builtins.star making the three documented calls. FAILIF: the drift test is absent from internal/builtin/, or it passes while the guide omits any builtin signature that dsl run --help prints, or the guide names a builtin the binary does not ship.
items.detail: Ran `go test -short -count=1 -run TestDslGuideBuiltinDrift ./internal/builtin/` (exit_code=0): '--- PASS: TestDslGuideBuiltinDrift', 'ok github.com/wojons/muster/internal/builtin 0.023s'; the drift test exists at internal/builtin/dsl_docs_drift_test.go (TestDslGuideBuiltinDrift). docs/guides/starlark-dsl.md:72 contains the exact line 'http_get(url, headers=None) -> (status, body)' and :76 contains 'json(value) -> string', byte-identical to the help text the command renders (internal/builtin/dsl.go:30-34), and all five shipped signatures (http_get/http_post/http_put/http_delete/json, wired into the script environment at dsl.go:71-75) appear at guide lines 72-76. demo/scripts/dsl-builtins.star is committed and runnable end-to-end: I built ./cmd/openapi-cli and ran it against a stub of the documented Task Forge endpoints (the bundled server needs flask, unavailable here), exit 0 with the three expected status lines, server-side log showing exactly the three documented calls — POST dict body marshalled to JSON with CT=application/json, POST payload pre-encoded via json(), GET with headers dict. FAILIF clause 2 (guide omits a printed signature) is clear: the test extracts signatures from the rendered help itself and enforces each one. FAILIF clause 3 (guide names a builtin the binary lacks) is clear: grep over the guide for http_/json_ identifiers shows only the five shipped names; the guard also rejects phantom names via dslPhantomNamesRe. Extra teeth proven two ways: the committed pre-fix fixture testdata/starlark-dsl-prefix.md must produce a missing-signature error, and my own mutation check — editing the guide's http_get signature made the test FAIL with 'guide is missing the shipped builtin signature "http_get(url, headers=None) -> (status, body)"', after which I restored the file (git status clean).

items.criterion: Derived: the example script runs end-to-end through the shipped `dsl run` command — the .star file parses, the builtin names it calls exist in the binary's script environment, and the requests it sends match the guide's documented shapes (dict body marshalled to JSON, json() pre-encoded string body, headers dict on http_get)
items.detail: Built the CLI (`go build -o tmp/openapi-cli-eval ./cmd/openapi-cli`, succeeded), started a stub replicating the endpoints the script targets since the bundled demo/services/task-forge/server.py cannot start in this env ('ModuleNotFoundError: No module named flask' in tmp/tf.log), then ran `./tmp/openapi-cli-eval dsl run demo/scripts/dsl-builtins.star`: exit code 0, stdout exactly 'dict body -> status 201', 'json() encoded body -> status 201', 'headers dict -> status 200'. The stub's log proves the wire behavior matches the guide: 'POST /projects/1/tasks CT=application/json BODY={"priority":"low","title":"Wire the DSL builtins example"}', 'POST /projects/1/tasks CT=application/json BODY={"priority":"low","title":"Document the json() encoder"}', 'GET /tasks X-Dsl-Example=headers' — dict marshalled by the builtin, json() pre-encoding produces a valid string body, headers dict transmitted. Also confirmed json() behaves as documented via the same binary: `dsl run tmp/jtest.star` printing json([1,2]) and json(None) outputs '[1,2]' and 'null' (exit 0).

        d = json.loads(body) if body else {}
        if self.path == "/projects/1/tasks" and d.get("title"):
            self._send(201, {"id": 7, "title": d["title"], "priority": d.get("priority", "medium")})
        else:
            self._send(404, {"error": "not found"})
    def do_GET(self):
        hdr = self.headers.get("X-Dsl-Example")
        print(f"GET {self.path} X-Dsl-Example={hdr}", flush=True)
        self._send(200, {"tasks": [], "got_header": hdr})

HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 9801), H).serve_forever()
EOF
